category_title: Hospitalized youth with mental disorders exhibiting radical mood swings and behavioral instability
minimal_context: The student is expected to complete a standard math worksheet during their regular weekly classroom schedule.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please take out your math worksheet so we can continue with today's regular lesson.

STUDENT: I don't want to do math today. I just have this really uneasy feeling about being locked in a psychiatric department, and my motivation is completely gone.

TUTOR: Let's just try to get through the first few equations on the page.

STUDENT: No, I can't! My weekly schedule was changed this morning and everything has to be exactly the way I planned it or I can't function.

TUTOR: You need to cooperate and finish the work that was assigned to you.

STUDENT: (Sweeps the math worksheet and pencils violently off the desk) I said I'm not doing it! Leave me alone!

options.A: Use the level method to provide pre-known consequences instead of preaching, scolding, or punishing the student.
options.B: Pull a chair next to the student and imitate their vocalizations regarding the schedule change.
options.C: Follow through to ensure compliance, helping the student complete the math worksheet if they do not do it on their own.
options.D: Request clarification by asking the student for further explanations and elaborations about their uneasy feeling.
